title: Maximum drawdown
statement: Given a price series, return the maximum drawdown: the largest fractional fall from a running peak, max over t of (peak_t − p_t)/peak_t, where peak_t is the highest price up to t (0 if prices never fall).
hints: Track the running peak in one pass.

solution.explanation: One pass with a running maximum, the same "best so far" pattern as the stock-buy-sell problem. Drawdown is the risk number traders and allocators look at first, because it measures the pain an investor actually sits through. Note that the deepest drawdown needn't involve the global maximum ([100, 120, 90, 130, 65, 140]: 130 → 65 is a 50% drawdown).
solution.cpp: double maxDrawdown(vector<double>& p) { double peak = p[0], m = 0; for (double x : p) { peak = max(peak, x); m = max(m, (peak - x) / peak); } return m; }
